Method of Attack: UEFI bootkit planted in system firmware, invisible to OS security software
Integrated Secure Boot bypass using vulnerable signed bootloader
Starts in recovery or safe mode
Anti-virtual machine (anti-VM), anti-debug, and code obfuscation features to block malware analysis
Runs under SYSTEM account within legitimate process to evade detection
Disables Windows security protections such as Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity (HVCI) and Windows Defender
Can load unsigned drivers enabling Bring Your Own Driver (BYOVD) attacks
Discoverer: Kaspersky lead security researcher Sergey Lozhkin
Attack Vector: UEFI firmware via vulnerable signed bootloader exploiting Secure Boot bypass vulnerability
Indicators of Compromise: Advertisement and promotion on hacking forums and criminal forums (KELA's Dark Beast platform)
